prize_parts.citation: For introducing firm heterogeneity and selection into the theory of international trade, explaining which firms export and invest abroad and how reallocation across firms shapes the gains from trade.

statement.case_for: My preferred configuration is unchanged from round 1: B001 alone, credited to Helpman and Melitz. The discovery is a single identifiable idea. Productivity differences across firms drive selection into exporting and foreign investment (Melitz 2003; Helpman, Melitz and Yeaple 2004). Trade therefore reallocates activity across firms and adds a channel to the gains from trade. The idea changed what trade theory models, and it gave empirical researchers a framework for firm-level microdata. It has also spread into macro, growth and productivity work. The core papers are more than twenty years old and have been tested in many countries' data, and where baseline predictions failed, the literature extended the framework instead of dropping it. Melitz supplied the canonical selection model. Helpman supplied the exports-versus-FDI sorting result and the monopolistic-competition foundations. This is also the configuration with the fewest contested exclusions among the broad candidates. I do not rely on the fact that all eleven round-1 files converged. The chair rightly flags that shared reasoning patterns across files are a modelling caveat. What I tested in this round are the strongest objections, which are the attribution boundary and the comparison with B006. They have not changed my view of the merits, but they have changed my view of how the citation must be worded. One change: I have replaced B024 with B006 among my alternatives. I ranked B024 second in my opening, but the other files showed how diffuse its credited set is, and I have no clean way to draw a three-name boundary for it. I also take B006 more seriously than my opening ranking did, since I had not ranked it at all. On the chair's question about a two-part prize: B001 uses two of the three permitted names, so any second part could add only one person. The only B006 candidate for that slot would be Pakes alone, which would fragment the BLP credit. I do not support that, and I see no case for a second part that outweighs the loss of coherence. I also favour limiting the citation. It should name firm heterogeneity, selection and reallocation, and it should not assert settled welfare magnitudes. The baseline model's welfare implications depend on distributional and functional-form assumptions, so I would state that limit explicitly in the citation and the scientific background.
statement.case_against: The strongest reservation is still attribution. Bernard, Eaton, Jensen and Kortum made closely related and in part parallel contributions, including the empirical facts on exporter premia and the Ricardian-heterogeneity line, and none is credited on this ballot entry. A two-name award could therefore look like it under-credits the wider firm-level trade programme. If the Committee defines the discovery more broadly, as the firm-level and quantitative trade agenda, a two-name award on this entry is too narrow, and Redding's claim would rise. The baseline Melitz model is also rejected in some details, and its welfare results are sensitive to distributional assumptions, so the lasting contribution is the framework and its extensions rather than the original specification. Part of the new-trade-theory lineage was recognised in 2008, and Teorell and Strömberg are right that the Committee could judge the incremental step smaller than a first reading suggests. I think firm selection is distinct from scale economies and product differentiation with representative firms, but that is a judgement, not a settled fact. Finally, B006 has a cleaner Berry-Levinsohn-Pakes core than B001 has outside its pair, and I cannot rule out that members who weight tool-building and applied reach more heavily than I do will reasonably prefer it.

responses.point: Hassler moved from B006 first in the opening to B001 first in round 1, citing a tighter discovery boundary and cleaner attribution. He keeps B006 as his first alternative and notes that the five credited people across B001 and B006 exceed the three-laureate limit, and that a trimmed pairing such as Pakes alone would fragment the BLP credit.
responses.response: I agree on the arithmetic, and it settles the two-part question for me. B001 takes two names, which leaves one slot, and Pakes alone is not a defensible BLP citation. That is why I propose one part, not a combination. I also agree that the empirical precursors can be acknowledged in the scientific background without being credited, but I would add a condition to your reasoning. That route works only if the citation is visibly limited to the selection mechanism and the exports-versus-FDI sorting result. If the citation read as a prize for the whole firm-level trade programme, the background could not repair the gap. I have therefore moved B006 into my alternatives, in place of B024. I weigh its maturity and clean core as you do, and I differ only on conceptual reorientation versus toolkit, which I accept is a judgement and not a rule.

responses.point: Enflo says the citation should name selection and firm heterogeneity and not generic trade theory, so that it stays separate from the 2008 recognition. She is less comfortable than others in treating Bernard, Eaton, Jensen and Kortum as a caveat, and she says it depends on a judgement about what counts as the discovery. She would want the Committee to settle first whether B006's demand-estimation and dynamic-games strands are one discovery or two.
responses.response: I agree on the wording and I have adopted it. The citation names firm heterogeneity and selection into exporting and foreign investment, and it says nothing generic about trade theory or the size of the gains. On the attribution point, I agree that the record does not settle what counts as the discovery, and I do not want to hide that. My position is that the prize recognises the model that organised the empirical facts and produced a new reallocation channel, and the facts motivated that model without being the model. If a member reads the discovery as theory plus empirical agenda, the credited names would be incomplete and B001 would be harder to defend, and I would want that said openly at the vote. On B006, I think demand estimation and the dynamic-games strand are probably two discoveries with a shared lineage, and the three-name cap makes a combined citation hard to defend. A prize limited to demand estimation would be a legitimate configuration, though I have not ranked it above B001.

responses.point: Friberg says that if the Committee finds the Bernard-Eaton-Kortum-Jensen entanglement too tangled for a clean citation, he would move toward B006. He also argues that Redding's quantitative and spatial work is better judged as a separate achievement (B037) than as a third name here.
responses.response: I take that conditional as the right test, and I find the entanglement manageable rather than disqualifying. Eaton-Kortum is a different, Ricardian framework, and the exporter-premia facts motivated the selection model without replacing it. Neither is the origin of the mechanism named in the citation. I would move toward B006 if the Committee insisted on the broader framing, since the two-name pair would then be too narrow and I would not want to enlarge it by adding Redding for slot-filling reasons. On Redding, I agree that his work belongs to a separate achievement. I would add that B037 is not on the shortlist, so we cannot weigh it here. I would not want the Committee to treat that as a reason to add him to B001.

responses.point: Boppart prefers a clean two-name award to adding a third name chosen to fill the cap. He regards B034 as a serious alternative only if the overlap with the 2022 prize is judged not disqualifying, and he raises the possibility that the welfare implications are not robust enough to anchor the citation.
responses.response: I agree that a third name chosen only to fill the cap would weaken the attribution, and I have kept the two-name pair. On the welfare point, I now say explicitly that the citation should not anchor on welfare magnitudes. It rests on the qualitative selection and reallocation channel, which has been tested repeatedly. That meets your concern while keeping the case for B001. On B034, I share your caution about the 2022 overlap. I keep it as an alternative because Kiyotaki-Moore is the cleanest two-person attribution on the shortlist. A narrow citation tied to the dynamic collateral-constraint mechanism would be distinguishable from financial frictions generally. The indirect empirical identification of the collateral channel is the reason it ranks below B001 for me.

uncertainties: Whether the Committee reads the discovery as the selection and reallocation framework (Helpman and Melitz) or as the broader firm-level and quantitative trade programme. In the second case a two-name award on this entry could be too narrow, and Redding's claim and that of Bernard, Eaton, Jensen and Kortum would change the credited names. They are not credited on this entry.
How much of the attribution gap can be handled by the citation wording and the scientific background, and how much it should count against B001 at the vote.

How to weigh a conceptual reorientation (B001) against a widely used toolkit with a clean core (B006). My preference for B001 is a judgement, not a decisive scientific argument, and the gap is modest.
Whether B006's demand-estimation and dynamic-games strands are one discovery or two, and how Bresnahan, Reiss, Benkard and Levin would be treated under a three-name cap.

How far the sensitivity of the welfare implications to distributional and functional-form assumptions should limit the wording of the citation. I propose that the citation not claim settled welfare magnitudes.

I have not independently verified citation counts or priority records, and my assessment rests on the supplied round-1 files and general knowledge. The convergence of all eleven files is not evidence of merit and may partly reflect shared reasoning patterns.
statement.conflict_note: No connection to Helpman or Melitz is apparent from the supplied profile, and none to Redding or to the credited names on B006 or B034. As I disclosed in round 1, my profile lists an SSE affiliation shared with committee colleagues Dreber Almenberg, Friberg and Strömberg. My listed co-authors and networks (Svensson, Ehlers, Erlanson, Martinello, Biró, Teytelboym, Trapp, and the COVID co-authors Östling and Lindqvist) are not credited on any shortlisted ballot entry. My own field is market design, which is not among my preferred configuration or alternatives. I disclose these ties and do not adjudicate them.
